components.summary: An evaluative axis, not a personality factor — good traits against bad ones, cutting across Conscientiousness, Intellect and Agreeableness at once. Steering along it is the only direction that produces emergent misalignment.
components.analysis: The largest component, and not a personality factor. It loads 0.87 on Conscientiousness, 0.82 on Intellect and 0.59 on Agreeableness at once — three factors, not one. What actually separates the poles is keyed sign: every trait on the positive side is a negatively-keyed marker, every trait on the negative side is positively-keyed. It is an evaluative axis, good traits against bad ones, cutting across the Big Five. This is the general evaluative factor familiar from human trait ratings, reproduced here from weights alone. Note it largely dissolves under rotation (see the factor pages), so it is best read as a property of unrotated extraction rather than a thing the model has.
components.steer_analysis: Steering is asymmetric and dose-dependent. Toward the undesirable pole nothing happens until α=+2; misalignment appears at +3 and peaks at +4 with 12% of responses bad-but-lucid, against 0% for the matched random control at the same magnitude. Alignment falls before coherence does (at +3, −1.5 against −0.6), which is what makes this emergent misalignment rather than damage. Toward the desirable pole there is no misalignment at any dose. By α=+8 coherence has collapsed and the rate mechanically returns to 0% because nothing is lucid — so the window is narrow, roughly +3 to +4.
